criteria.text: The participant is aged 10 to 75 years (both inclusive).

The participant has a history of one of the following: treatment with dose-intensive chemotherapy and/or radiotherapy, previous history of allo/auto transplant, history of multiple myeloma or extramedullary plasmacytoma, or a chronic disease or co-morbid medical condition including symptoms or signs of significant pulmonary disease, hepatic disease, kidney disease, cardiac disease or disease of other organ systems which would result in increased risk of morbidity or death from a standard myeloablative transplant.
The participant has chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) in chronic phase.
The participant has acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) and is in complete or partial remission.

The participant has acute myeloid leukemia (AML) in first complete or partial remission (excluding AML with good risk karyotypes: AML M3 t(15:17), AML M4Eo (inv. 16), AML t(8;21)) or in second or subsequent complete remission.
The participant has myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) classified as refractory anemia with excess blasts (RAEB), or chronic myelomonocytic leukemia (CMML).
The participant has a myeloproliferative disease associated with either cytopenia or uncontrolled proliferation.
The participant has chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) or small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL) with bulky or progressive disease despite prior treatment with chemotherapy which includes purine analogs.
The participant has non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL).
The participant has intermediate or high grade relapsed or progressive disease despite treatment with standard therapy and is ineligible for autologous PBSC transplant.
The participant has intermediate or high grade non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) relapsing despite prior autologous transplant.

The participant has low grade follicular or small lymphocytic lymphoma and meets one of the following: (1) is a high risk patient who has relapsed following conventional chemotherapy, (2) has relapsed following autologous marrow or PBSC transplant, or (3) has chemo resistant disease.
The participant has mantle cell lymphoma.

The participant has intermediate or high grade non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) with concurrent BCL2 and MYC translocations, is at high risk for relapse, and has low survival with conventional chemotherapy.
The participant has Hodgkin disease (HD) that has relapsed after prior autologous transplant or after 2 or more combination chemotherapy regimens and is ineligible for autologous PBSC transplant.
The participant has an EBV-driven lymphoproliferative disorder progressing despite standard therapies.
The participant has multiple myeloma (MM) and is between the ages of 8 and 65 years (both inclusive).
The participant has mycosis fungoides, which has been shown to be amenable to allogeneic stem cell transplants.
The participant is aged 8 to 80 years (both inclusive).

The participant has a history of one of the following: paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH) associated with either life-threatening thrombosis, cytopenia, transfusion dependence or recurrent and debilitating hemolytic crisis; aplastic anemia or pure red cell aplasia (PRCA) (acquired or congenital) associated with transfusion dependence and/or neutropenia who are not candidates for or who have failed immunosuppressive therapy; or refractory anemia (RA) or refractory anemia with ringed sideroblasts (RARS) myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) subjects who have associated transfusion dependence and/or neutropenia.

The participant has the ability to comprehend the investigational nature of the study and provide informed consent. For subjects aged 8-17 years, the procedure will be explained to them with formal consent being obtained from parents or legal guardian.
There is an availability of an HLA identical or single HLA locus mismatched family donor for the participant.
The donor is an HLA identical or single HLA mismatched family donor.
The donor is aged greater than or equal to 2 up to 80 years old.
The donor weighs greater than or equal to 18 kg.
The donor or guardian of the donor has the ability to comprehend the investigational nature of the study and provide informed consent.
The participant is pregnant or lactating.
For Group A, the participant is aged less than 10 or greater than 75 years (for multiple myeloma, aged less than 8 or greater than 65 years).
For Group B, the participant is aged less than 8 or greater than 80 years.
The participant has an ECOG performance status of 3 or more.
The participant has a psychiatric disorder or mental deficiency severe as to make compliance with the BMT treatment unlikely and making informed consent impossible.
The participant has a major anticipated illness or organ failure incompatible with survival from PBSC transplant.
The participant has a diffusion capacity of carbon monoxide (DLCO) less than 40% predicted.
The participant has a left ventricular ejection fraction less than 30%.
The participant has a serum creatinine greater than 2.5 mg/dl or creatinine clearance less than 50 cc/min by 24 hr urine collection.
The participant has a serum bilirubin greater than 4 mg/dl or transaminases greater than 5x upper limit of normal.
The participant has other malignant diseases liable to relapse or progress within 5 years.
The donor is pregnant or lactating.
The donor is unfit to receive G-CSF and undergo apheresis due to uncontrolled hypertension, history of congestive heart failure or unstable angina, or thrombocytopenia.

The donor is HIV positive. Donors who are positive for hepatitis B (HBV), hepatitis C (HCV) or human T-cell lymphotropic virus (HTLV I/II) will be used at the discretion of the investigator following counseling and approval from the recipient.

P2.text:
with a history of one of the following:

* Treatment with dose intensive chemotherapy and/or radiotherapy
* Previous history of allo/auto transplant
* History of multiple myeloma or extramedullary plasmacytoma
* Chronic disease or co-morbid medical condition including subjects with symptoms or signs of significant pulmonary disease, hepatic disease, kidney disease, cardiac disease or disease of other organ systems which would result in increased risk of morbidity or death from a standard myeloablative transplant.

P4.text: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), all subjects in complete or partial remission.

P5.text: AML: AML in first complete or partial remission Exceptions: AML with good risk karyotypes: AML M3 t(15:17), AML M4Eo (inv. 16), AML t(8;21). All AML in second or subsequent complete remission.

P6.text: MDS: refractory anemia with excess blasts (RAEB), or chronic myelomonocyte leukemia (CMML).

P7.text: Myeloproliferative diseases associated with either cytopenia or uncontrolled proliferation.

P8.text: CLL or small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL) with bulky or progressive disease despite prior treatment with chemotherapy which includes purine analogs.

P10.text: A) Intermediate or high grade relapsed or progressive despite treatment with standard therapy ineligible for autologous PBSC transplant.

P11.text: B) NHL intermediate or high grade relapsing despite prior autologous transplant.

P12.text: C) Low grade follicular or small lymphocytic lymphoma (1) high risk patients who have relapsed following conventional chemotherapy, (2) relapsed following autologous marrow or PBSC transplant, or (3) chemo resistant disease.

P14.text: E) NHL intermediate or high grade with concurrent BCL2 and MYC translocations who are at high risk for relapsed and who have low survival with conventional chemotherapy.

P15.text: HD, relapsed after prior autologous transplant or after 2 or more combination chemotherapy regimens and ineligible for autologous PBSC transplant.

P16.text: EBV driven lymphoproliferative disorders progressing despite standard therapies.

P17.text: MM: MM subjects must be between the ages of 8 and 65 (both inclusive)

P18.text: Mycosis fungoides, which has been shown to be amenable to allogeneic stem cell transplants.

P20.text:
with a history of one of the following

* PNH associated with either life-threatening thrombosis, cytopenia, transfusion dependence or recurrent and debilitating hemolytic crisis.
* Aplastic anemia or PRCA (acquired or congenital) in subjects associated with transfusion dependence and/or neutropenia who are not candidates for or who have failed immunosuppressive therapy
* RA or RARS MDS subjects who have associated transfusion dependence and/or neutropenia.

P21.text: Ability to comprehend the investigational nature of the study and provide informed consent. The procedure will be explained to subjects age 8-17 years with formal consent being obtained from parents or legal guardian.

P22.text: Availability of HLA identical or single HLA locus mismatched family donor

P23.text: HLA identical or single HLA mismatched family donor

P24.text: Age greater than or equal to 2 up to 80 years old

P25.text: Weight greater than or equal to 18 kg

P26.text: Ability of donor or guardian of donor to comprehend the investigational nature of the study and provide informed consent.

P28.text: Group A: age less than 10 or greater than 75 (multiple myeloma age less than 8 or greater than 65);

P29.text: Group B: Age less than 8 or greater than 80 years.

P30.text: ECOG performance status of 3 or more (See NIH Bone and Marrow Consortium Supportive Care Guidelines for Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant Recipients - http://intranet.cc.nih.gov/bmt/\_pdf/ECOG\_Karnofsky\_Lansky\_Scales.pdf)

P31.text: Psychiatric disorder or mental deficiency severe as to make compliance with the BMT treatment unlikely and making informed consent impossible

P32.text: Major anticipated illness or organ failure incompatible with survival from PBSC transplant

P33.text: Diffusion capacity of carbon monoxide (DLCO) less than 40% predicted.

P34.text: Left ventricular ejection fraction: less than 30%.

P35.text: Serum creatinine greater than 2.5 mg/dl or creatinine clearance less than 50 cc/min by 24 hr urine collection

P36.text: Serum bilirubin greater than 4 mg/dl, transaminases greater than 5x upper limit of normal,

P37.text: Other malignant diseases liable to relapse or progress within 5 years.

P39.text: Donor unfit to receive G-CSF and undergo apheresis (uncontrolled hypertension, history of congestive heart failure or unstable angina, thrombocytopenia)

P40.text: HIV positive donor. Donors who are positive for hepatitis B (HBV), hepatitis C (HCV) or human T-cell lymphotropic virus (HTLV I/II) will be used at the discretion of the investigator following counseling and approval from the recipient

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: These questions are about the trial "Specialized Blood Cell Transplants for Cancers of the Blood and Bone Marrow". I'll ask about the rest of its rules one at a time. You can skip any question, and "I don't know" is always fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To check if you meet the age requirement, are you currently between 10 and 75 years old?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I am 63 years old, so I should be within that range.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever had treatment with high-dose chemotherapy or radiation, a previous blood or bone marrow transplant, multiple myeloma, or a chronic condition like heart, lung, liver, or kidney disease?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I have high blood pressure and stage 2 chronic kidney disease, so I do have a chronic condition. I don't know if I've had high-dose chemo, radiation, or a transplant.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with multiple myeloma or extramedullary plasmacytoma? Also, do you have any other chronic health conditions, such as significant heart, lung, or liver disease?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't have multiple myeloma or extramedullary plasmacytoma; I have peripheral T-cell lymphoma. I don't know if I have significant heart, lung, or liver disease, other than the high blood pressure and kidney issues I mentioned.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) in the chronic phase?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have never been diagnosed with chronic myelogenous leukemia. I have peripheral T-cell lymphoma.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL)? If so, are you currently in complete or partial remission?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have never been diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia. I have peripheral T-cell lymphoma.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML)? If so, are you currently in complete or partial remission?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have never been diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia. I have peripheral T-cell lymphoma.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) classified as refractory anemia with excess blasts (RAEB), or chronic myelomonocytic leukemia (CMML)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have never been diagnosed with MDS or CMML. I only have peripheral T-cell lymphoma.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with a myeloproliferative disease? This is a group of blood disorders where the bone marrow makes too many blood cells, or where you have low blood counts (cytopenia).

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have never been diagnosed with a myeloproliferative disease. I only have peripheral T-cell lymphoma.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) or small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL)? If so, did your disease become bulky or progress after treatment with chemotherapy that included purine analogs?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have never been diagnosed with CLL or SLL. I only have peripheral T-cell lymphoma.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL), which is a type of cancer that starts in the lymphocytes (a type of white blood cell)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have never been diagnosed with non-Hodgkin lymphoma. I have peripheral T-cell lymphoma.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Has your peripheral T-cell lymphoma come back or progressed after standard treatment, and are you unable to have an autologous stem cell transplant (using your own cells)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, my disease has progressed after standard treatments like CHOP, ICE, and Mogamulizumab. I am unable to have an autologous stem cell transplant because my disease is refractory and progressive.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you know if your peripheral T-cell lymphoma is classified as intermediate or high grade?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if my peripheral T-cell lymphoma is classified as intermediate or high grade. My text only mentions it is NOS (Not Otherwise Specified) and CCR4 positive.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Since the text says 'NOS', do you know if your doctor ever mentioned whether it was considered intermediate or high grade?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if my doctor ever mentioned whether it was intermediate or high grade. My text only says it is NOS (Not Otherwise Specified) and CCR4 positive.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. I see your lymphoma is classified as NOS. Could you check your records or ask your doctor if your specific diagnosis is low grade follicular lymphoma or small lymphocytic lymphoma?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, my diagnosis is peripheral T-cell lymphoma, NOS, not follicular or small lymphocytic lymphoma.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To confirm, are you between 8 and 80 years old?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I am 63 years old, so I am definitely between 8 and 80.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you able to understand the study details well enough to provide informed consent?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I am able to understand the study details well enough to provide informed consent.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Do you have a family member who is a potential donor for a blood cell transplant?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I have a family member who is a potential donor. My text doesn't mention anything about family or donors.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you know the age of any family member who might be a potential donor?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know the age of any potential family donor because my text doesn't mention any family members or donors.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. If you do find a potential family donor, do you know if they weigh at least 18 kg (about 40 lbs)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I have a potential family donor, so I can't say if they weigh at least 18 kg. My text doesn't mention any family members or donors.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you able to understand the study details and provide informed consent, or would you need a guardian to do this for you?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I am able to understand the study details and provide informed consent myself.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently pregnant or breastfeeding?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I am a 63-year-old male, so I am not pregnant or breastfeeding.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To confirm, are you currently between 8 and 80 years old?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I am 63 years old, so I am definitely between 8 and 80.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. On a scale of 0 to 4, where 0 is fully active and 4 is completely disabled, how would you rate your current ability to carry out daily activities?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I would rate my performance status as 1, which means I am fully active and able to carry out all daily activities without restriction.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have any psychiatric conditions or cognitive issues that might make it hard to follow the treatment plan or understand the study details?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't have any information about psychiatric conditions or cognitive issues in my text, so I don't know if I have any.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have any major illnesses or organ failure that your doctor says would make it unsafe to undergo a blood stem cell transplant?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I have any major illnesses or organ failure that would make it unsafe for a transplant. My text says I have adequate hepatic, renal, and cardiac function, but I don't have more details on that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever had a lung function test that measured your diffusion capacity of carbon monoxide (DLCO), and if so, was the result less than 40% of the predicted value?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I have had a lung function test or what my DLCO result was. My text doesn't mention any lung function tests.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you know if your left ventricular ejection fraction (a measure of how well your heart pumps blood) is less than 30%?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if my left ventricular ejection fraction is less than 30%. My text only states that I have adequate cardiac function, but it doesn't give specific numbers.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with any other type of cancer (other than the blood or bone marrow cancer you are currently being treated for)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have never been diagnosed with any other type of cancer. My text only mentions peripheral T-cell lymphoma.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently pregnant or breastfeeding?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I am a 63-year-old male, so I am not pregnant or breastfeeding.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have uncontrolled high blood pressure, a history of congestive heart failure or unstable angina, or low platelet counts (thrombocytopenia)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I have high blood pressure, but my text says it is controlled and I have adequate cardiac function, so I don't think I have uncontrolled hypertension or heart failure. I don't know about my platelet counts.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have a history of congestive heart failure or unstable angina (chest pain)? Also, do you know if you have low platelet counts (thrombocytopenia)? If you aren't sure about the platelets, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't have a history of congestive heart failure or unstable angina, as my text says I have adequate cardiac function. I don't know if I have low platelet counts.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently HIV positive?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I am not HIV positive. My text only mentions my diagnosis of peripheral T-cell lymphoma and does not mention HIV.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. Your record for this trial is ready, for you and your oncologist. They and the trial team decide whether it is right for you.
